NEW DELHI: Air India Express suspended eight crew members for three months for failing to complete the mandatory post-flight declaration, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.The incident took place on August 2 after the flight landed in Amritsar from Dubai.According to ANI, the crew was required to undergo the post-flight declaration within two hours of landing. However, they were delayed by 35 minutes and submitted the declaration after two hours and 35 minutes."As per the airline’s mandatory rules for testing of psychoactive substances, all crew members underwent the test, and the reports came negative," sources told ANI."The entire incident was reported to the DGCA, and the airline decided to suspend the eight crew members for three months," they added.According to DGCA rules, crew members operating international flights for Indian carriers must complete a post-flight alcohol test within two hours of landing in India, regardless of individual circumstances during that window.

Article Title: Govt debunks Pakistan claim that IAF MiG-29 crashed during landing due to pilot error
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The press information bureau (PIB) fact check unit on Thursday debunked a social media claim that an Indian Air Force (IAF) MiG-29 fighter jet had crashed during landing due to pilot error. They stated that the video being circulated was footage from a video game.The fact-checking unit warned that the video was being circulated by Pakistani propaganda accounts and called the claim fake.“Pakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a video with the claim that an IAF MiG-29 fighter jet crashed during landing due to pilot error,” PIB Fact Check said in a post on X, adding, “Beware! This claim is #Fake.”The unit said the footage was from War Thunder, a military combat video game featuring aircraft, land and naval vehicles.The video circulating on social media shows a fighter jet crashing while attempting to land, followed by the pilot ejecting and parachuting to safety. The footage was presented online as an actual IAF MiG-29 crash by certain accounts based out of Pakistan.PIB Fact Check urged users to report suspicious content related to the Government of India through its official channels.The claim is part of a recurring pattern of propagandist accounts circulating unrelated military accidents and video-game footage are circulated as evidence of recent events.
Article Summary: Pakistani propagandists run video game footage as iaf crash purportedly due to pilot error. Video circulating on social media shows fighter jet crashing while attempting to land, followed by the pilot ejecting and parachuting to safety. Article Title: 'See how many allies of Pakistan were in that room': Omar Abdullah praises Centre over Pahalgam condemnation at Brics

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday heaped praise on the foreign policy of PM Narendra Modi-led Centre and recently held Brics Summit in Delhi. Omar Abdullah said the Brics declaration condemning Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack was a major diplomatic win.J&K CM remarks came after India hosted the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi, bringing together several world leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.The National Conference leader particularly highlighted the inclusion of the Pahalgam terror attack in the Brics New Delhi Declaration, pointing out that the statement came in the presence of countries that share close ties with Pakistan."That is something for the Government of India, and particularly for the foreign ministry, to talk about. The fact that Pahalgam itself was condemned is a big thing. Please see how many allies of Pakistan were in that room. Therefore, for even Pahalgam to be mentioned by name, that in itself is a success of our foreign policy," Omar Abdullah said.J&K CM Omar also welcomed steps aimed at easing tensions along India’s fronts with Pakistan and China.Reacting to the ministry of defence’s report on the operational situation along the Northern Front, he said any move to reduce troop deployments along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) or Line of Control (LoC) would be a positive development, particularly for people living in border areas."Anything that reduces tension along the Line of Control or the Line of Actual Control is a good step, particularly for those people who live close to it. We know that living near the LoC or LAC is extremely difficult for people. If there is any step that reduces deployments along the Line of Actual Control, that is a good step. Similarly, we hope that, over time, things will also get better along the Line of Control," he added.The comments came days after the Brics Summit concluded in the national capital. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the New Delhi Declaration had been unanimously adopted and called the gathering as a huge summit.Days ago, senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor backed the Brics Summit as an important diplomatic opportunity for India, appearing to differ with party colleague P Chidambaram, who questioned whether recent Brics meetings have produced tangible benefits.Tharoor highlighted the diplomatic value of India hosting leaders from across the Brics grouping and its partner countries, stressing the importance of such engagements for New Delhi.Chidambaram, however, had questioned the outcomes of recent Brics summits.“I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results.”“In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics Summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.Chidambaram’s remarks triggered a political response from the BJP, which accused the Congress of questioning an event that, it said, reflected India’s growing standing on the global stage.
Article Summary: Omar praises centre for brics declaration condemning pakistan-backed pahalgam terror attack. J&k cm omar also welcomed steps aimed at easing tensions along india’s fronts with pakistan and china. Comments came days after the brics summit concluded in the national capital.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah backed Centre's decision to introduce 0.4 percent merchant discount rate on UPI payments above Rs 2,000, saying that "running a UPI system" is not cheap.While talking to reporters, Omar said that people don't appreciate what they "get for free.""Not everyone is charged. First of all, person-to-person money transfers are not charged. After that, individual consumers will not be charged unless they cross a certain ceiling limit. As far as I understand, running this UPI system is not cheap. It takes a lot of money to run it. And the truth is, we don't properly appreciate what we get for free," J&K CM said."The government should ensure that the general public is not charged these fees. If a company is charged, I have no objection because companies make good money through UPI anyway," he added.This comes after the opposition raised concerns over the rollout of UPI charges, alleging that the cost would ultimately be borne by common citizens.Earlier on Wednesday, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi targeted the centre and accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of putting a on every single person by “taxing UPI".“Modiji has a completely diff concept, he's neither left or right he has decided to completely lie down straight and in front of Donald Trump. He's put a tax on every single Indian person by taxing UPI and giving huge amount op money to the United States,” the former Congress president added.The new MDR will take effect from October 15. However, UPI payments between individuals, including transfers made to friends, will not be charged, according to the Centre.Responding to the critics and concerns over the new framework, the Union finance ministry said banks were asked to ensure merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. “UPI application providers are expressly prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges".

Article Title: ‘May your service be accompanied by good health’: Bangladesh PM Rahman wishes PM Modi on birthday
Article Text:

Greeting from across nation and beyond

NEW DELHI: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman wished Prime Minister Narendra Modi on his 76th birthday on Thursday, as Dhaka seeks to reset ties with New Delhi.“Warmest birthday wishes to Prime Minister @narendramodi. Wishing you many happy returns of the day. May your dedicated service to the people of India always be accompanied by good health and high spirit,” Rahman posted on X.PM Modi responded by thanking Rahman for his message.“Thank you, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, for your warm wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words,” he said.The exchange comes at a time when Bangladesh is seeking to move away from the strained ties of the previous 18 months. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Sunday that Dhaka wanted to “reset” its relationship with India and establish a new engagement centred on mutual interests.Relations had deteriorated during Muhammad Yunus’s interim administration, which came to power after the Sheikh Hasina government was toppled in August 2024. Hasina left Bangladesh for India after her ouster, and her continued stay there has remained a major point of friction, with Dhaka repeatedly seeking her extradition.Rahman’s Bangladesh Nationalist Party won the February 12 election, held without Hasina’s Awami League, which has since been disbanded. His government has maintained its demand for Hasina’s extradition, while the former prime minister has said she plans to return to Bangladesh to face legal proceedings.Dhaka has also indicated that Rahman could visit India once the two governments agree on a suitable time and schedule.Rahman’s message was among birthday greetings sent to PM Modi by political leaders, foreign governments, diplomats and public figures on Thursday.Russian President Vladimir Putin sent his wishes and, according to the Russian Embassy in New Delhi, described PM Modi as a leader with “great authority on the global stage”. Putin also thanked Modi for the “warm and cordial welcome and hospitality” during his recent visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit.Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the Prime Minister as a “friend” and said she looked forward to further strengthening India-Italy relations. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Modi’s leadership had “transformed India into a world power” and described the India-Israel relationship as an “unprecedented partnership”.The US Embassy in India also conveyed birthday greetings on behalf of President Donald Trump.Opposition leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mayawati and Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, joined the birthday wishes.PM Modi was born on September 17, 1950, in Vadnagar, Gujarat. He became Gujarat chief minister in 2001 and prime minister in 2014, and is set to complete 25 years in public office on October 7.The BJP has launched a month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ to mark the occasion, with service and public outreach programmes across the country. In Delhi, about 1.25 lakh earthen lamps were lit at Kartavya Path as part of the ‘Ashirwad Ka Diya’ campaign.Several film personalities, including Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, Chiranjeevi, Ram Charan, Mahesh Babu and Kamal Haasan, also wished the prime minister.

The exchange comes at a time when bangladesh is seeking to move away from the strained ties of the previous 18 months. JAMMU: A special NIA court in Jammu has issued non-bailable warrants (NBWs) against two Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commanders for evading arrest in terror cases.Justice Prem Sagar passed separate orders on Sept 8 against the duo — Khalid alias Lala Huzaifa alias Bakkarwali, a resident of Pakistan’s South Punjab province; and Saifullah alias Sajid Jatt alias Ali Bhai alias Habibullah Malik (also known by several other aliases), a resident of Pakistan’s Kasur district.NIA alleged that Khalid and Saifullah had worked as LeT commanders in Kashmir before moving to Pakistan, from where they were currently providing weapons, money, and directions to ultras operating in Kashmir. While Khalid was active in Ganderbal and Bandipora districts, Saifullah — a designated terrorist listed in the Fourth Schedule of UAPA — operated in Kulgam between 2005 and 2007, NIA stated. The investigation also revealed communication IDs allegedly linked to Saifullah, according to court records.The proceedings stem from a case wherein J&K Police intercepted a motorbike at Gujar Tent, Pandach, Srinagar, during naka checking on March 31, 2026. A Chinese grenade and 15 live rounds/cartridges were allegedly seized from the rider, Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat of Batpora, Srinagar. An FIR was registered at Zakoora PS under provisions of the UAPA, Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act. The case was transferred to NIA in April.DSP Amit Sharma said NIA moved applications before the special court seeking NBWs against Khalid and Saifullah. As their attendance could not be secured through ordinary means, the court granted the requests. The NBW against Khalid was forwarded to DIG, NIA Jammu, for execution, while Saifullah’s NBW was sent to SSP Kulgam.

Article Title: Sohar emerges as India’s gateway to GCC as Hormuz crisis reshapes shipping
Article Text:
Sohar Port sees a 400% rise in India feeder services as Hormuz crisis reshapes shipping routes to GCC markets.

NEW DELHI: Since the conflict in West Asia disrupted shipping through Strait of Hormuz, Oman’s Sohar Port has emerged as a key gateway for Indian exporters shipping cargo to Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. Feeder vessel services between India and Sohar have increased by nearly 400%, reflecting a shift in regional trade routes, a top Sohar Port executive said.GCC comprises Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Since the crisis, several shipping lines have rerouted services to ports located east of Strait of Hormuz, including Salalah, Khorfakkan, Sohar and Jeddah.Responding to a question from TOI, Sohar Port deputy CEO Raid Al Rubaiey said the port has seen a sharp rise in food and consumer cargo from India.“A lot of foodstuff is now coming through Sohar and other GCC ports. We are seeing significant volumes of rice and other food products from India. Many Indian products that earlier moved on large vessels through Strait of Hormuz are now coming via Sohar. The frequency of feeder vessels between India and Oman has increased fourfold,” he said.Rubaiey added cargo arriving at Sohar from India and other countries is being transported by road to destinations across GCC, strengthening the port’s role as a regional distribution hub.With cargo volumes rising, Sohar Port is expanding its handling capacity to position itself as “the gateway for India to the GCC”, he said. He added that the port is in discussions with several Indian terminal operators that have expressed interest in operating facilities at Sohar, as the port looks to deepen its logistics partnership with India.

Article Title: 'Fundamental national responsibility’: India's envoy to US strikes defiant note as Trump's 100% tariffs loom
Article Text:
India’s Ambassador to the United States

India’s Ambassador to the United States Vinay Mohan Kwatra has defended New Delhi’s energy sourcing policy after the US House of Representatives passed legislation that gives US president Donald Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries continuing to buy Russian oil and gas, including India and China. The bill was approved 262-159 after clearing the Senate last month and now goes to Trump for signature.In an X thread titled “People First: What Drives India’s Energy Imperative”, Kwatra said India’s energy choices were driven by development and energy security.“Energy is a vital strategic necessity for 1.4 billion Indians and a foundation of our development….India is the world’s fastest-growing major economy and its third-largest energy consumer. Yet the average Indian consumes less than one-third of the global average and one-tenth of average American. Our energy needs will, and must, grow,” he said.Kwatra said reliable and affordable energy was essential for homes, farms, hospitals, schools, factories and transport.“India imports over 85% of its crude oil and around half its natural gas. Our sourcing reflects a fundamental national responsibility: looking outside our borders to secure adequate, affordable and uninterrupted energy for our people,” he said.He added that India sources energy from partners across the Middle East, Africa, Latin America, Eurasia and the US, with decisions guided by “availability, affordability, market conditions and commercial viability”.“When recent conflicts squeezed global supplies, India acted decisively to protect its people from price shocks. That also helped steady global energy markets and prevent a deeper crisis. The energy security of India’s people comes first!” Kwatra said.The Ministry of External Affairs said India had noted the passage of the legislation and was monitoring further developments. It reiterated that New Delhi remained committed to energy security through diversified sourcing and evolving market conditions.The MEA said, “The Indian side has also made clear its determination to take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests,” adding that the government would work with Indian trade and industry bodies to address the implications.The legislation comes amid wider trade tensions between India and the US. Further bilateral trade discussions are expected on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers’ meeting in Wisconsin later this month, as negotiations on a broader trade agreement continue.
Article Summary: The us house of representatives passed legislation that gives us president donald trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries continuing to buy russian oil and gas. The bill was approved 262-159 after clearing the senate last month and now goes to trump for signature.

Article Title: Mid-sea collision: Pak vessel was no match to three-times bigger Indian destroyer INS Kolkata
Article Text:
Pakistan's PNS Hunain sustained significant damage after colliding with India's INS Kolkata.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: When 2600-tonne Pakistan warship PNS Hunain collided with Indian Navy ’s 7400-tonne destroyer INS Kolkata, three times its weight, on Tuesday evening, the outcome was known as the Pakistani vessel was no match to India’s big warship. The Pakistan offshore vessel was severely damaged and had to return to the harbour whereas, Indian sources said, the Indian destroyer suffered no damage in the collision.In a statement on Thursday, Pak govt said its “Navy was undertaking its biennial exercise SEASPARK-26 when the Indian vessel carried out aggressive manoeuvres in dangerously close proximity to a Pakistani naval ship, resulting in contact between the two vessels”. Its foreign ministry, in a tit-for-tat reaction on Thursday, summoned the Charge d'Affaires of the Indian High Commission in Islamabad and lodged a strong protest.However, Indian defence sources told TOI that it was the “Pakistani ship that closed the Indian warship on a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea at high speed, manoeuvring in an unprofessional and unsafe manner that led to the collision”.Visuals emerging showed PNS Hunain a huge dent on it and the warship had to be sent for repairs. PNS Hunain is aYarmook-class patrol vessel designed for maritime security, surveillance and limited combat capabilities. Commissioned in 2014, PNS Hunain is about 98 metres long.On the other hand, INS Kolkata is 164 metres long and has a maximum speed of 30 knots and is the lead ship of the indigenously designed and constructed Kolkata-class guided missile destroyers. It carries a heavy mix of surface-to-air missiles, anti-ship cruise missiles, rapid-fire guns, and anti-submarine weapons like BrahMos missiles, Barak 8 missiles and close-in weapon system. For anti-submarine warfare, the Indian warship has torpedo launchers, rocket launchers and a bow-mounted sonar system.PNS Hunain would have sunk if INS Kolkata had taken offensive action. “However, despite extreme provocation, the captain of INS Kolkata “had exercised extreme restraint by taking actions to prevent a severe accident from taking place,” the source told TOI.
Article Summary: Pakistan's pns hunain sustained significant damage after colliding with india's ins kolkata. The pakistan offshore vessel was severely damaged and had to return to the harbour. Indian sources said, the indian destroyer suffered no damage in the collision.

Article Title: 'Your leadership has transformed India into a world power': Netanyahu greets PM Modi on 76th birthday
Article Text:
Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu

Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday extended birthday greetings to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, describing the India-Israel relationship as an “unprecedented partnership” and saying the friendship between the two countries had “never been stronger”.Birthday greetings poured in from across the world, with foreign leaders, envoys and diplomatic missions highlighting India’s bilateral partnerships and Modi’s role in strengthening ties. Russian president Vladimir Putin praised his contribution to the “special and privileged strategic partnership” between India and Russia, while Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni wished Modi “health, energy, and success”.“Happy birthday, Narendra!” Netanyahu wrote in a post on X, alongside an image of the two leaders. “Your leadership has transformed India into a world power. Together, we have built an unprecedented partnership between our two great democracies.”The Modi-Netanyahu bonhomie has become a prominent feature of India-Israel ties, with both leaders repeatedly highlighting their personal friendship and political trust.Their meetings and public exchanges have highlighted a relationship that extends beyond formal diplomacy into close strategic cooperation.“The friendship between Israel and India has never been stronger, and together we will take it to even greater heights,” he added, wishing Modi “many more years of leadership, health and fulfillment”.India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992, while PM Modi’s July 2017 visit to Israel elevated the relationship to a strategic partnership. Netanyahu followed with a visit to India in January 2018.The relationship now covers defence, security, technology, agriculture, water, innovation, trade and other areas. During PM Modi’s visit to Israel in February 2026, Netanyahu described him as “my dear friend” and said, “You are more than a friend; you are a brother in many respects.” He also said, “Israel is stronger than ever and India is stronger than ever.”Netanyahu's birthday message came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where the grouping adopted a New Delhi Declaration that included strong references to the Israel-Lebanon conflict and the Gaza war.On Lebanon, BRICS leaders said, “We welcome the ceasefire in Lebanon” and called for full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701. The declaration also called on Israel to “withdraw its occupying forces from all of the Lebanese territories, in which they remain”.That diplomatic contrast has not, so far, translated into a visible rupture in India-Israel ties. Netanyahu’s latest message instead points to continued political engagement, while New Delhi maintains separate tracks with Israel, Arab countries and the wider BRICS grouping.

Article Title: '9/11 architects were not hiding in caves': India hits out at Pakistan at UN over terror safe havens
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit out at Pakistan at the UN Security Council, saying Islamabad had provided a "permissive environment" to the "architects" of the 9/11 attacks and continues to provide space and support to terror groups such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed.Speaking at a UN Security Council meeting, India's Permanent Representative P Harish recalled the 9/11 terror attacks in United States and said al-Qaida leaders Osama bin Laden and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed were eventually found in settled communities in Pakistan rather than "caves or badlands".“The international community supported the global campaign to counter terrorism in the wake of 9/11. Let us not forget, however, that al-Qaida's terror ecosystem established its strategic depth beyond Afghanistan through its affiliates,” Harish said.“The leaders of al-Qaida who conceived and directed these 9/11 attacks did not escape justice in the wilderness of some ungoverned frontier.”The Indian envoy also listed out the names of terrorists found in Pakistan.Bin Laden, who ordered and financed the 9/11 plot, was “tracked down and killed in a fortified compound within a settled, guarded community under Operation Neptune Spear”, he said.Mohammed, “the principal architect of the operation, was found sheltering in an ordinary residential house.Ramzi Binalshibh, who coordinated the hijacker cell after being denied a visa to join them, was sheltering in an urban centre,” Harish said.Senior al-Qaida operative Walid bin Attash, who helped select and prepare several hijackers, was captured separately, while Mustafa Ahmed al-Hawsawi, a key financial and logistical facilitator of the 9/11 operation, was also captured in Pakistan, he said."In each case, these were not fugitives hiding in caves or badlands, they were men who had long evaded detection. Draining this swamp that provided an enabling environment for such monsters of humankind to prosper is important," Harish said, in a thinly veiled reference to Pakistan.Harish also drew attention to what he described as an axis involving Pakistan, al-Qaida and terrorists targeting India."The same permissive environment that sheltered the architects of 9/11 has, in the years since, continued to provide space, support, and impunity to affiliates of al Qaida such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed and their like," he said.He said these groups continue to operate under different identities to evade the Council's sanctions, while their terror-training infrastructure continues to operate with impunity.The international community must act against the continued existence of such sanctuaries, he said, "to ensure that more such individuals are not thrust upon any country or its citizens and no one loses family and loved ones".Last week, as the world marked 25 years of the September 11 terror attacks perpetrated by al-Qaida, UN Security Council members, including Pakistan, visited the 9/11 memorial in Lower Manhattan.

Article Title: Houthis, Saudis, Iran - and the future of Middle Eastern oil
Article Text:
Houthi fighters stand in front of what they say is a downed Saudi jet, at a location given as Yemen

What’s the latest Houthi offensive all about?

Why is this a serious headache?

Why now?

Why are Saudis in a jam?

What are the takeaways?

In a lightning offensive last week, Yemen’s Houthis took over much of the country’s Red Sea coast, threatening shipping in the vital sea lane that had emerged as an alternative to Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf. Houthis have been fighting a Saudi-led military coalition for a decade, although a 2022 UN-brokered truce halted their attacks on Saudi territory. But the Houthis’ latest move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark, adding another front to the wider US-Israel war against Iran. Here’s the lowdown on why the Houthis’ Red Sea threat matters, how this puts Saudi Arabia in a serious pickle, and what it means for the Iran war:The offensive saw Houthis take over key parts of Yemen’s Red Sea coast. This adds weight to the Houthi threat to shipping in the vital sea lane. In fact, Houthis had earlier declared a blockade of Saudi ships in the region. Now they can seriously enforce this. Their mere presence along the coastline will make shippers jittery and raise insurance costs.With Strait of Hormuz effectively locked up by Iran and US, Red Sea had emerged as a vital alternative route, especially for energy trade out of the region.Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline was working at full capacity, transporting around 7 million barrels of oil daily across the breadth of the peninsula to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. This was a crucial lifeline for the global energy trade that had been severely restricted following the outbreak of the Iran war in Feb. But that East-West pipeline was hit by a drone attack last week — blamed on Iran-backed Shia militias in Iraq — to coincide with the Houthi advance on the Red Sea coast. Both operations seem to have been coordinated to put the choke on Red Sea shipping, which has to pass through the narrow Bab el-Mandeb strait that Houthis can now theoretically shut down.The timing of all this is not a coincidence. Actually, when the Iran war began, among Iran’s proxies in the region, Houthis held back. But in July, following the state funeral of Iran’s former supreme leader Ali Khamenei, an Iranian plane carrying the Houthi delegation back to Yemen was threatened by Saudi Arabia. Riyadh did not want that plane to land, and bombed the airport in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital of Sanaa. But that plane landed anyway.Following the episode, Houthi rhetoric against the Saudis flared up. But the key development that may have pushed Houthis into action could be the American blockade of Iranian ports and shipping in Persian Gulf.By many estimates, that blockade appears to be working, and putting enormous pressure on the Iranian economy. Tehran is unable to push out its own oil, the Iranian rial has tanked, and Iranians have actually taken to saving eggs instead of hard cash. Plus, this is a strategy that plays into America’s strength — it can carry out a naval blockade for a far longer period than a continuous kinetic war against Iran.So, Iran, through the Houthi action, is sending the message that if oil can’t pass through Hormuz, any alternative routes, including through the Red Sea, will also be shut. In short, the energy trade in the region is handcuffed till the war is resolved.What do Houthis want? The Houthis’ main grievance is against the Saudis, whom they have been fighting since 2015. But, of course, as a member of Iran’s so-called ‘Axis of Resistance’, they are now being heavily supported by Tehran in terms of material and intelligence inputs. Especially since the Gaza and Iran wars have seen Tehran’s two main proxies in Hezbollah and Hamas take a huge battering. So, the Iranian Axis appears to be undergoing a recalibration, with Houthis and Iran-backed militias in Iraq taking a more leading role among the proxies. Ultimately Houthis want legitimacy. Their attacks against Saudi Arabia — they reportedly fired a drone at Mecca earlier this week — raise their profile. Their capture of the Red Sea coast gives them international attention. And these, in turn, see them emerge as the primary force in Yemen, instead of the internationally backed Yemeni transition govt. Obviously, all of this helps Iran.Because US has refused to directly intervene against Houthis this time. Washington is providing diplomatic and advisory support to Riyadh, but not much else. Saudis want missile and drone interceptors. But US stocks are running low, thanks to its war with Iran. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has similarly sought assistance from Egypt and UK. But no one is rushing military aid to Riyadh. Interestingly, even the recently inked Mecca Pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan hasn’t been activated.First, Houthis prove Iran’s Axis of Resistance is changing shape, with the Yemini militia taking a leading role. This has implications for both the Iran war, and security in Red Sea and Horn of Africa region. And second, alternative routes to Hormuz for energy transit, whether through sea or pipelines, are also not fully secure. They can be targeted by a host of Iran-backed militias in the region. This puts West Asia’s dominance in global energy supply under a serious cloud, perhaps forcing the international community to look for alternatives away from the region.
Article Summary: Houthis have been fighting a saudi-led military coalition for a decade. The houthis’ latest move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark. Houthis had earlier declared a blockade of saudi ships in the region. Houthis prove iran’s axis of resistance is changing shape, with the yemini militia taking a leading role.
